transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi, yeah, thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate you taking the time. Um... I hope I'm doing this right, but I guess I came in because a few people have been pointing out some things about how I've been acting. It's a little embarrassing, honestly, but I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

They've been telling me that they can actually see me moving... I don't know, just really slowly. Almost like I’m underwater? Like, it'll take me forever just to answer a question or even get up out of a chair. It's probably just me being tired, but... well, then other times it's the exact opposite. I'll just be pacing around my apartment, constantly rubbing my hands together like I’m trying to shake off a really bad customer service call. 

I know that probably sounds a bit strange, I'm sorry. Is that... is that the kind of thing you need to know?

During these times when you feel slowed down or, on the other hand, restless and pacing, how would you describe your mood—are you feeling sad and down, unusually high or irritable, or mostly anxious and worried?

Um, that's a really good question. I hope I can explain it right. I guess I'd say I've been feeling mostly... sad? I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining, because I know everyone gets down sometimes. But yeah, most of the time since all this started, there's just been this... this sadness kind of hanging around in the background. 

Along with that, I've been feeling pretty guilty about things, and just... not really having much interest in my usual hobbies. Plus my sleep has been a bit off. It's all just sort of always there in the background, you know? Though, I mean, some weeks are definitely lighter than others, so it's not like it's unbearable all the time. I try my best to just push through it and stay positive at work. 

Does that... does that answer your question okay? I can try to be more specific if you need me to be.
Have you ever gone through a period—separate from feeling sad—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and felt like your thoughts were racing?

Um... no, I don't think I've ever really had anything like that. Honestly, I kind of wish I had a little more energy sometimes! But no, I don't get super elated or have racing thoughts, and I definitely always feel like I need sleep, even if I'm struggling to actually get it. 

I've never really had a time where I felt super charged up or irritable in the way you're describing. I hope that's okay? I know sometimes people have a mix of both, but for me it's really just the feeling down part. Am I explaining that alright?
Have you noticed any recent changes in your memory, confusion, or new medical problems—like a head injury, illness, or new medication—around the time these slow or restless episodes started?

Um, no, nothing like that. I haven't hit my head or been sick or anything. And I'm not taking any new medications, just some over-the-counter stuff for headaches sometimes, but that's it. 

As for memory or being confused... I mean, I guess I can be a little forgetful sometimes, but nothing major. Just the normal kind of forgetting where you put your keys, you know? I really try hard to stay organized at work, so I haven't noticed any big problems with my memory or anything. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out.
How long has this sadness and these ups and downs in your energy been going on—would you say it's been at least two weeks straight?

Um, well... I guess it's been a lot longer than two weeks, actually. I hope it's okay to admit that. I've been trying really hard to just manage it on my own, so I haven't really talked about how long it's been going on. 

But, um, if I really think about it, the feeling down part... it's been going on for about two years now. Maybe two years and a month? I mean, there are definitely times where it eases up a little bit, just brief periods where I feel a bit lighter, so it's not like I'm completely miserable every single second of the day. I really try to keep a good attitude, especially for my job. But yeah, the sadness has pretty much been there for a couple of years. 

Is that... is that helpful to know? I hope I didn't wait too long to get help. I just didn't want to make a big deal out of it if it was something I could just push through, you know?
Over these past two years, has there ever been a stretch of at least two weeks where your sadness and other symptoms became noticeably worse or more intense than your usual day-to-day baseline?

Um, well... I don't really think so? Like, I try really hard not to let things get out of hand. So it's mostly just been that same, um, steady kind of low feeling I mentioned. 

I mean, sure, maybe I'll have a bad day here or there where I feel a little extra tired, but I always make sure to pull myself together, especially so I can do my job well. I don't think I've ever let it get super intense or noticeably worse for two whole weeks straight. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, I'm really doing my best to manage it and keep things on an even keel, so I hope I'm giving you the right information here. Does that make sense for what you're asking?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a chronic, low-grade depressive mood lasting approximately two years, with associated guilt, anhedonia, sleep disturbance, and psychomotor changes (alternating slowing and agitation). Symptoms are persistent but do not reach the severity or represent a distinct change from baseline consistent with a major depressive episode—no discrete 2-week period of marked worsening was identified despite chronicity. No manic/hypomanic history, and no medical/substance etiology (no head injury, illness, or new medications) was found to explain the psychomotor symptoms. This presentation is most consistent with Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia), F34.1, rather than Major Depressive Disorder or a mood disorder due to another medical condition.
